title: AR display power vs thermal ceiling in eyewear
bottleneck: A glasses temple is a sealed, skin-contact enclosure with almost no heat-spreading capacity, yet displays and SoCs demand watts to render bright, high-resolution AR. Sustained compute for on-device vision models adds more heat with nowhere to go. The thermal ceiling forces throttling, dimming, or bulky designs that defeat the purpose of glasses.
why_it_blocks: Heat is the silent killer of all-day AR: it caps brightness, compute, and battery life simultaneously. Every AR glasses design is a negotiation with physics that current technology loses.
current_state: Display-less AI glasses achieve all-day wear precisely by removing the display stack; display models manage only a few hours. Active cooling in eyewear is impractical. Sustained on-device AI workloads add compute heat on top of display heat, forcing throttling within minutes of intensive use.
